# Lucky Numbers in a Matrix. compare: unordered 0; with distinct numbers a
# matrix has at most one lucky number, so every answer has 0 or 1 values.

@example 11 is the smallest number of its row [15,11,14] and the largest of its column [3,11,9].
[[12,3,7],[15,11,14],[2,9,6]]
=> [11]

@example Every row's smallest number is in the first column, and 8 is the largest number there.
[[5,20],[8,30],[1,40]]
=> [8]

@example The row minimums 4, 1 and 5 are beaten in their columns by 7, 10 and 8, so none is lucky.
[[4,9,6],[2,1,8],[7,10,5]]
=> []

# A single number is lucky.
[[7]]
=> [7]

# One row: its smallest number is lucky, since each column holds one number.
[[9,3,100000,4]]
=> [3]

# One column: its largest number is lucky.
[[2],[100000],[1],[50]]
=> [100000]

# The smallest matrix with no lucky number.
[[1,4],[3,2]]
=> []

# Values at the bounds, and no lucky number.
[[100000,1],[2,99999]]
=> []

# The lucky number is in the top-left corner.
[[50,60,70],[10,80,90],[20,30,40]]
=> [50]

# The lucky number is in the bottom-right corner.
[[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[10,11,9]]
=> [9]

# A wide matrix: the lucky number is in the last column.
[[8,9,10,11,7],[1,2,3,4,5]]
=> [7]

# A tall matrix: the lucky number is in the last row.
[[1,60],[2,70],[3,80],[40,90],[50,55]]
=> [50]

# A wide matrix with no lucky number.
[[1,5,6],[4,2,3]]
=> []

# A tall matrix with no lucky number.
[[6,1],[2,5],[4,3]]
=> []

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[[20,14,18],[1,13,4],[17,7,9]]
=> [14]

@gen 2 small
[[13]]
=> [13]

@gen 3 small
[[1,7,13],[4,10,2],[11,3,17],[5,18,12]]
=> []

@gen 4 small
[[10,6,19],[2,1,9],[17,15,18],[11,3,13]]
=> [15]

@gen 5 small
[[2,3],[20,15]]
=> [15]

@gen 6 small
[[19,2],[8,7]]
=> [7]

@gen 7 small
[[8,6,7],[15,13,11]]
=> [11]

@gen 8 small
[[4,15,10,13],[3,5,12,2],[6,20,11,8]]
=> [6]
